crm_notes:
- Company background: Neon Harbor is an e-commerce personalization platform powering product recommendations and conversational support across 6 retail brands.
- Primary ask: cut latency and inference cost for live chat & on-site personalization. Cost sensitivity high (optimizing gross margin).
- Perf targets discussed: 95th percentile chat latency target <= 120ms at sustained 100 qps; embeddings batch throughput target 5000 reqs/min; cost target ~ $50k–$120k ARR on initial rollout.
- Model preferences: open-models preferred (Llama-like family, Mistral variants) with ability to pin and fallback to smaller quantized variants.
- Architect notes from SE call: enable continuous batching for low-latency bursts, aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeated session turns, and per-route batching windows. Want automated suggestions from Redwood Optimize for batch size + cache TTL.
- Quantization: trial int8 + nvq8 profiles; need regression monitoring (quality delta threshold) and rollback. SE asked for Redwood examples of quantize + eval pipeline.
- Routing/fallback: multi-variant routing by latency tier (hot / warm / cold); fallback to smaller model if latency SLO threatened. Must support region-aware routing (NA primary, EU residency for EU customers).
- Security/compliance: SSO/SAML integration mandatory, SOC2 baseline, per-token audit logs, KMS for key management, and data residency enforcement for EU shoppers.
- Quote from CTO: "We can't sacrifice perceived latency for savings — shoppers abandon after 300ms perceived lag." Wants benchmark data that reflect production traffic (burstiness + cold-starts).
- Documents & artifacts: shared perf trace, Redwood perf template, security FAQ link.
- Sales notes: good champion in Head of Product; procurement timeline aligned to April. AE pushing for Dedicated POC to demonstrate unit economics and latency profile.
